question.text:
CASE STUDY (Continued): Mr. Sharma's investments: Investment 1: Equity MF - profit Rs. 3,00,000 (held 15 months) Investment 2: Debt MF - purchased Feb 2024, profit Rs. 50,000 (held 8 months) Investment 3: ELSS - profit Rs. 80,000 (held 4 years) Investment 4: IDCW of Rs. 8,000 received
Question 3: What is the tax treatment of Mr. Sharma's ELSS profit (Investment 3)? Calculate the tax including cess, considering that Investment 1 and Investment 3 gains are combined for the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption.

answer.text: Rs. 10,400 (12.5% on Rs. 80,000 with separate Rs. 1.25 lakh ELSS exemption + 4% cess)
Nil - ELSS gains are fully exempt since investment qualifies under Section 80C
Rs. 10,400 (ELSS is equity-oriented, so LTCG at 12.5% on Rs. 80,000 + 4% cess, as Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption already used against the larger equity MF LTCG)
Rs. 24,960 (30% slab rate on Rs. 80,000 + 4% cess, since ELSS is taxed at slab after lock-in)

explanation.text: The Logic: ELSS is an equity-oriented fund. After the 3-year lock-in (Mr. Sharma held 4 years), gains qualify as long-term capital gains on equity-oriented schemes and are taxed under the Section 112A framework at 12.5%. The Rs. 1.25 lakh annual LTCG exemption is a combined limit across all equity LTCG of a single investor in a year. Since Investment 1 already produces Rs. 3,00,000 of equity LTCG, the entire Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption is consumed there. So the ELSS LTCG of Rs. 80,000 is fully taxable. Tax = 80,000 x 12.5% = Rs. 10,000. Health & education cess at 4% = Rs. 400. Total = Rs. 10,400. The Trap: Option A wrongly assumes a separate ELSS-specific Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption. Option B confuses Section 80C deduction (on amount invested) with exemption on gains; 80C does not exempt capital gains on redemption. Option D applies a slab rate to ELSS LTCG, which is incorrect — ELSS is equity-oriented and follows the equity LTCG rate, not slab. Note: The cited workbook (NISM V-A, pp.157, 161-162) supports ELSS being equity-oriented with a 3-year lock-in and Section 80C deduction, and supports the Rs. 1.25 lakh equity LTCG exemption, but the explicit 12.5% LTCG rate and 4% cess are not stated on those pages. The rate and cess figures above reflect general current Income Tax Act treatment of equity LTCG under Section 112A.
